subject: Kestrel AI — throughput surge, elevated error rate & request for SLA credit / remediation
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@kestrel-ai.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@kestrel-ai.com, security@kestrel-ai.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2027 09:14:00 -0000
Subject: Significant throughput spike + 5xx rate - request for exec call and credit

Irene —

We saw a major surge in latency and a ~7% 5xx rate across our production routes yesterday and again this morning. That resulted in timeouts for several customer workflows and a spike in error retries from our side. We've attached our incident logs and a short summary.

Immediate asks:
- Exec-level sync today if you have availability (we're based in PST)
- A provisional calculation for SLA credit while you investigate (we need a number to provide to procurement)
- Confirmation on containment timelines and whether there's a plan to prevent recurrence during our December traffic window

This problem is impacting our paid customers and internal SLAs — we're elevating it to procurement and security. Please cc the right folks on your side.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Product, Kestrel AI
samira@kestrel-ai.com

Attachment: kestrel_incident_log.zip (attachment stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@kestrel-ai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Significant throughput spike + 5xx rate - request for exec call and credit

Samira — thanks for the escalation and the logs. I'm very sorry for the impact here.

Short answers up front: we can do an exec call today at 16:00 PST; we'll prepare a provisional SLA credit calc and an initial containment plan.

I'll loop in engineering (Dylan) for root cause and a mitigation runbook, and Marissa/Laura for commercial and procurement coordination.

Proposed agenda for the call (30m):
- Incident summary and customer impact (Kestrel)
- Our initial findings and mitigation steps (Redwood Eng)
- Provisional financial remediation proposal (Redwood Sales)
- Next steps & contract amendment path (legal/finance follow-up)

I will send a calendar invite; please let me know if anyone else on your side should join.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0194

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2027 15:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Significant throughput spike + 5xx rate - request for exec call and credit

Irene / team — quick technical summary to prep for the call and the provisional credit calc: 

What we observed:
- Sudden upstream traffic pattern change at 02:40 UTC that caused hot-shard contention on the inference routing layer; request fanout increased 3x for short windows (~10–30m)
- Under that load, a combination of KV cache eviction behavior and an edge retry storm produced elevated latency and ~7% server-side 5xx rate for affected routes
- Failover to a lower-capacity pool occurred but with degraded throughput due to quantization mismatch on fallback instances

Immediate mitigations applied (already deployed):
- Rate-limit throttle for anomalous traffic patterns (reverted bad client-side retries)
- Adjusted cache TTL heuristics to reduce evictions during bursts
- Short-term routing change to avoid the smallest quantized instances for Kestrel's critical routes

Next steps (72h):
- Full hot-shard remediation and improved fanout limits (engineering ticket KES-321)
- Post-mortem with perf traces and primers for your SREs
- A suggested runbook for your side to avoid retry amplification in the short-term

I'll bring timing estimates to the call. Attaching the mitigation runbook and the per-route error graphs for your review.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Attachment: mitigation-runbook.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2027 08:20:00 -0000
Subject: INTERNAL: Kestrel escalation — provisional credit calc & contract remediation options

Team — after reviewing the logs and Dylan's notes, Kestrel is asking for a provisional credit they can give procurement this week. We should be conservative but avoid over-committing. Summary: ~4 hours of degraded service (varied by route) across the month; revenue at risk is estimated at $64k for the impacted period per Kestrel's report.

Options for a provisional commercial offer (pick one to present on the call):
A) One-time credit = 20% of impacted monthly invoice (provisional) + expedited remediation priority (no additional fee)
B) One-time credit = 40% of impacted monthly invoice + 90-day remediation SLA with weekly checkpoint and financial penalties for repeat breach
C) No immediate large credit; accelerated engineering support + capped service credit (10%) after post-mortem verification

Requirements for anything above 10%: legal/finance must sign off on contract amendment language and DocuSign path. Marissa, Laura — can you have a draft amendment and an editable spreadsheet for the credit calc before the call? Vivek — can you join the exec call if option B is on the table?

Also flagging KES-321 as high priority in the backlog; engineering ETA for full remediation estimate expected within 48–72 hours.

Irene

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@kestrel-ai.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2027 10:00:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Significant throughput spike + 5xx rate - request for exec call and credit

Samira — thanks for raising this and for the logs. We can take the exec call at 16:00 PST today.

On the provisional credit: based on our spreadsheet (attached) and Dylan's mitigation notes, our recommendation to present is Option B (40% provisional credit of the impacted monthly invoice) paired with a 90-day remediation SLA and weekly checkpoints. This reflects the severity and the risk to your customers during the surge window.

If Kestrel is comfortable with that, we'll prepare a short contract amendment to sign (DocuSign) that includes the remediation checkpoints and a clause for additional financial remedies if there's a repeat within 90 days. We can provide the editable calc now — see attached.

Marissa Cole
Account Director, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: sla-credit-proposal.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 16:42:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Kestrel escalation — sign-off and next steps

Team / Irene — I reviewed the notes, the provisional calc, and Dylan's proposed mitigations. I will join the exec call and am prepared to approve Option B as a one-time commercial remediation:

- Approve: 40% one-time credit of the impacted invoice (provisional)
- Approve: 90-day remediation SLA with weekly checkpoints. Engineering to include specific measurable targets (latency p50/p95 and 5xx rate thresholds) in the amendment.
- Condition: Contract amendment must include a clause that allows a further financial remedy if the same class of degradation recurs within 90 days. Legal to draft.

Laura / Marissa: please prepare the DocuSign amendment (use the HubSpot deal DL-78921), and include the editable credit spreadsheet. Finance — we should reserve funds for the provisional credit, label it as "service remediation reserve" in the accounting workflow so procurement has a point of contact.

I'll be on the call at 16:00 PST. Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial & Partnerships — Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123
